How to read this dashboard

Getting started (first time only)

1. Open the dashboard and approve the connectors it asks for: org62 (read-only, required), plus Slack, Google Calendar, Google Drive/Slides and Tableau for the full experience (Gmail and Lucid are optional). Then open Settings → Setup check and press Run all checks. 2. Check the "Viewing as" line next to the Today bar shows your name and team. 3. Click "⚙ Hours target" to set your own quarterly customer-related hours goal (default 250h). 4. Use "Log with Slackbot" or the Activity Editor to fix gaps the dashboard finds. 5. Click "Present" to build a Google Slides deck in your Drive, or "🎁 My year in review" for your fiscal year as a story. Nothing in org62 is ever changed by this page. If a number looks wrong, check "Data as of" and click ↻ Refresh first.

Where the numbers come from

Everything is read live from org62 (read-only). Your activity hours come from Events you logged. Your deal credit comes from Deal Contribution (DC) records, not the opportunity team. Queries are cached for 10 minutes; "Data as of" shows the oldest data on screen and Refresh forces new data.

Hours and Deals

Hours (Performance > Hours and activity) are split into customer-facing, customer-related and non-customer using the Global Activity Types guide. "Activity with no DC" means you logged meetings on an opportunity where you have no DC. "DC with no activity" means you hold a DC but logged nothing on it this quarter.

DC audit

Multiple 100% DCs per role: the GIC Playbook allows only one 100% credit per role on an opportunity. If you and another team member are both at 100% in the same role, that is a conflict, and one of you should lower the split. No customer hours: a DC where you logged no customer-related hours on that account in the last 12 months. It is a best practice, not a requirement.

Scoreboard

Deals closed counts closed-won opportunities where your team or you hold a DC, at full opportunity amount (so your deals also appear in the team number). Projected close adds open deals by forecast category (Commit, Best Case, Pipeline); Omitted deals are excluded. Weighted projection = closed won plus each open deal's amount times its stage probability. Win rate = won / (won + "Dead - Lost"); duplicates, webstore and similar are ignored. Slippage = open deals whose close date moved from this quarter to a later one.

Caveats

Credit numbers are not quota attainment: org62 quotas are not readable here. CCR quota lives in the Tableau CCR dashboard. Amounts are opportunity amounts, not booked ACV, and can differ slightly from finance reports.

How are deals recommended?
Open opportunities (next 12 months, $200K+) on your focus accounts and their related accounts where you have no DC. Services SOWs, renewals, webstore and spiff deals are excluded. Ranking uses your own logged time on the account family (Strong: 40h or more, Possible: 5h or more), your Slack and calendar work notes, then stage and amount. These are candidates only: confirm real involvement before adding. ＋ Add DC opens a pre-filled form (Technical Architect, 100%) and nothing is saved until you click Save in org62.
